findings:
I treated these as read-only maps and analysed them independently. Scripts, pickles and figures are in /n/home05/ianpoon/DNA-springs-project-2026-27/cryoEM/sfgfp_chimera_screening/results/tmp_review/a1/. The main figures are j56frame.png, j39frame.png, j53frame.png, pca_J51_J56_J61_J63.png and pca_J52_J39_J53.png.

**Methods.** Each map was low-passed with a Fourier filter to 12 Å and to 15 Å. Contours were set by enclosed volume (30k, 40k, 50k, 60k, 70k, 90k, 120k, 130k, 160k and 180k Å^3), plus thresholds chosen so the rods come out 18, 20 or 22 Å wide. At each contour I measured connected components and a medial longest path with its longest branch. I then fitted straight axes to each arm and measured arm ends where density along the axis falls to 50% and to 25% of the arm's own level. Lobes were measured as integrated excess density and as volume. Maps were compared by 6-D rotation and translation search (5,000 rotations x 2 hands, then local refinement), conical FSC on the half maps, view directions read from the J56/J61/J63 .cs files, and a half-split cross-correlation test for reference imprinting.

**Q1. What each map contains.** Every map is close to planar: its thickness along the third principal axis is about 20-30 Å.

- **J56** has one bright compact lobe D (peak about 10 times the rod level). Two rods leave D at only 24° to each other:
  - Arm DS runs straight to an end 90 Å from D's centre (95 Å by the 25% criterion). It is weaker towards its tip.
  - Arm DV is a full-strength rod to a node V, 72 Å centre to centre. V is a density maximum with almost no excess mass, so it is not a protein.
  - At V the path turns by 87° (88° and 86° in J61 and J63). The far arm VE then runs straight to an end 112 Å beyond V (121 Å at 25%), finishing in a small terminal lobe E.
  - The medial path from E through V to D is 190-214 Å over contours of 50k-160k Å^3, at both 12 and 15 Å. The kink sits at arc length 101-112 Å. The DS branch is 47-57 Å from where it joins the path.
- **J51** has the same topology with the same angles (87° and 26°) but shorter arms: VE ends 96 Å beyond V (103 Å at 25%) and DS ends 70 Å from D (85 Å at 25%). Its D lobe is relatively weaker against the rods. At contours of 40k-60k Å^3 the D/DV part separates from the far arm.
- **J52 and J39** agree with each other: refined CC 0.88 against a median of 0.32 over all rotations, from independent branches. Each has a straight rod 119-121 Å long by the 50% criterion (132-134 Å at 25%), as well as a compact blob 46-48 Å off the rod axis. The blob is placed at about 90° at one rod end. It is joined to the rod only weakly: the bridge is 22-38% of the rod level in J39 and 13-15% in J52. In J52 the blob is a separate component (7-12k Å^3) until the contour reaches 90k Å^3. J39 has its densest point at that corner; J52 does not.
- **J53** (reference-free, lone-dot-plus-haze particles) also contains rods, not just a dot:
  - an elongated dot whose half-maximum width is about 27 Å along its long axis;
  - a vertex 33 Å from the dot;
  - a 69° bend at that vertex;
  - a rod running 98-104 Å beyond the vertex, with a small extra stub.

  Its medial path is 155-199 Å. Its 6-D alignment to J56 is ambiguous (CC 0.755, with other poses at 0.75), and its geometry differs from J56 (33 Å versus 72 Å from dot to vertex).

**Q2. Is the far arm already in reference-free J51?** Yes. J51 and J56 are in the same frame: CC 0.87 in the native frame, and the global search gives the identity pose uniquely (0.92 against 0.83 for the next pose). Along the J56 node lines:

| Arm | J51 vs its own DV arm | J56 vs its own DV arm |
|---|---|---|
| VE | level 83%, linear integral 57% | linear integral 78% |
| DS | linear integral 88% | linear integral 102% |

So the kinked far arm with the same 87° angle is present without a reference. The three things that appear only after refinement are:
- arms about 16-20 Å longer (VE end at 96 Å becomes 112 Å; DS end at 70 Å becomes 90 Å);
- a terminal lobe at E, whose excess goes from -4 in J51 to +35 Å-of-arm in J56;
- a D lobe about twice as strong relative to the rods.

J51 is not independent of J56, though. J56 was started from a J51-derived class and shares particles with it.

J61 and J63 use the J56 poses unchanged (checked: poses, shifts and half-split assignments are identical). Their CC to J56 is 0.99. They contain no shared particles, yet they reproduce J56's arms, angles and arm ends to within 1-2 Å. J63's DV and DS arms are about 20% weaker relative to its dot, and its VE arm is equal. A direct imprinting test shows the poses carry the reference into any subset. In the 10-15 Å band, J61 half A against J63 half A correlates at 0.79. Both were aligned to the same J56 half-reference but share no particles. That is higher than J61 A against J63 B (0.64-0.65) and higher than the gold-standard halves within J61 (0.63). In the 15-30 Å band, where the arms are defined, every pair correlates at 0.99. So the near-identity of J61 and J63 says almost nothing about whether the haze particles really contain the arms. Any subset reconstructed with these poses would look like this. Only the reference-free J53 gives independent evidence, and it does show rods in the haze set.

**Q3. Common architecture?** There is a partial, suggestive match but not a distinctive one. Both families have a long straight segment (VE about 112-122 Å; free rod 119-134 Å) with a turn of roughly 90° about 112-134 Å from the free end, leading to compact density. But in J56 the turn leads through a full-strength rod 72 Å long to a strong lobe. In J52/J39 it leads through a weak bridge about 46 Å long to a weak blob. The free-rod maps have no DS arm. The 6-D search finds no unique superposition: best CC 0.68 for J52 and 0.65 for J39, with alternatives within 0.01-0.03.

Implied DNA path lengths:
- **J56:** from D's centre through V to the far end is 184-193 Å, so about 165-178 Å from D's surface. Over the contour scan it is 170-194 Å from D's centre.
- **J51:** 168-175 Å from D's centre, so about 150-160 Å from D's surface.
- **J56 total rod outside the dot:** DS, DV and VE together come to about 240 Å, roughly 1.4 times a 50 bp duplex.
- **Free rods:** 119-134 Å straight, or about 165-180 Å if the bridged blob is the DNA continuing round a hook.

Could the free-rod blob be an sfGFP? It cannot be excluded or confirmed. Its excess integral (21-22 Å-of-rod in an 18 Å sphere) is 0.3-0.45 of what a rigid, fully occupied sfGFP should give (50-78). Its volume at DNA-width contours (4.6-9.2k Å^3) is far below about 40k Å^3 for a simulated sfGFP at the matching threshold. Against the reference-free J51 dot (35-48 Å-of-rod excess, 5-6k Å^3), the blob has roughly 0.5x the integral and a similar volume. It would also fit about 6 bp of DNA, or a partially occupied or flexible protein.

**Q4. Is attached DNA shorter than 50 bp?** These maps do not show it shorter. The D-V-E path is about 150-178 Å from the dot surface, which is roughly 50 bp (about 166-170 Å). The free-rod straight segment is actually shorter (119-134 Å) unless its hook is counted. Whether D-V-E is a single continuous duplex cannot be decided at this resolution. The 87° kink is physically unexpected in intact B-DNA, and the extra rod (about 1.4 duplex-equivalents) shows that the arms cannot all be one 50 bp duplex in one particle. They are either two duplexes or averaged alternative positions. So the 3D maps neither confirm nor refute the earlier 2D finding that attached DNA is 16-33 Å shorter.

**Anisotropy check.** The J56 half maps give FSC 0.143 at 7.8 Å overall. In 30° cones it is 7.6 Å along the long arm, 8.9 Å along the in-plane perpendicular and 7.7 Å along the plane normal. J61 and J63 are 10.8 Å along the in-plane perpendicular. Views down the long arm are depleted (4-7% against 13.4% expected for uniform views), but there is no extreme top-view preference. The mild anisotropy should not change lengths or in-plane angles at the 12-15 Å scale. That does not overcome the reference-imprinting problem above.

**Self-skepticism.**
- The node coordinates came from peaks and visual inspection.
- The end criteria (50%/25%) are conventions; lengths move by about 5-15 Å between them, and the 12 Å and 15 Å results agree to within about 2 Å.
- The "Å-of-arm" mass units assume all rods are fully occupied and that DNA and protein give similar contrast per dalton (this alone is uncertain by a factor of 1.5-2).
- Planar objects are nearly unchanged by mirroring, so hand is undefined and does not matter here.

undecidable: Whether DS and D-V-E occur together in single particles (sfGFP carrying two duplexes) or are averaged alternative DNA positions. The total rod outside the dot is about 240 Å, roughly 1.4 duplexes, so they cannot all be one 50 bp duplex in one particle.
Whether the 87° turn at V is a real bend inside one continuous duplex, or two segments meeting (end-stacking, a second molecule, or overlapping conformers). V has almost no excess mass.

Whether the J56 dot is one sfGFP. Its integrated density is consistent with about 1 sfGFP if the arms are fully occupied, but its contoured volume is only about one third of a model sfGFP, and occupancy and contrast assumptions shift this by a factor of about 2.

Whether the free-rod blob is an sfGFP, a hooked DNA end (about 6 bp-equivalent) or noise. It measures 0.3-0.45 of the expected sfGFP signal, about 0.5x the J51 dot, and is only weakly bridged to the rod.
Whether the free-rod DNA path is 119-134 Å (straight segment only) or about 165-180 Å (counting the hook). This decides whether free rods are shorter than, or equal to, 50 bp.
The DNA length distribution from particle to particle. Half-maximum ends give an alignment-weighted population average, blurred by end flexibility and partial occupancy.

Whether the haze subset (J63) truly contains the arms. Reconstructing with J56 poses imprints the reference: the 15-30 Å band is identical for any subset, and the 10-15 Å band shows excess correlation between particle-disjoint subsets that share a half-reference. Only the reference-free J53 gives independent evidence, and its geometry differs from J56.
Whether the 16-20 Å extra arm length and the terminal lobe E in J56 (absent in J51) are real or produced by refinement. J51 and J56 are not independent.
Where on the dot the DNA attaches, and so the exact DNA length from the protein surface (taken here as 15-20 Å from the dot centre).
Out-of-plane geometry beyond about ±10 Å, and handedness. The objects are nearly planar, so mirror images look almost the same.

Whether a 50 bp duplex attached to sfGFP is 16-33 Å shorter, as the 2D analysis suggested. These maps are not shorter (attached path about 150-178 Å from the dot surface), but the 3D measurements cannot settle the question at 8-11 Å with mild in-plane anisotropy (10.8 Å in-plane-perpendicular cone in J61/J63) and with heterogeneity.

findings:
ANALYST 2: independent, read-only measurements. Scratch scripts and figures are in /n/home05/ianpoon/DNA-springs-project-2026-27/cryoEM/sfgfp_chimera_screening/results/tmp_review/a2/. The key figures are views12_zoom.png, paths_J56frame.png, profiles_J56paths.png and provenance.png.

METHOD. I low-passed every map to 12 Å and 15 Å with a raised-cosine filter. Contours were set by the volume they enclose (20k to 160k Å^3), because solvent sigma is meaningless in these flattened maps. Connectivity comes from peak finding plus a merge tree (the threshold at which two peaks join). Path lengths come from medial geodesic paths, smoothed. Rod ends are where density falls to half of the local rod plateau. I calibrated against simulated 12 Å maps of the sfGFP barrel (L6_protein.pdb with linkers removed) and of straight_50bp.pdb. The method gives 174-179 Å for a straight 50 bp duplex whose atoms span 171 Å, so it reads about 5 Å long. Maps were aligned by rigid-body cross-correlation (CC) search with both hands tested, and checked with an exhaustive search over 6000 rotations.

All the maps are essentially flat. The thinnest dimension at the 90k contour is 35-47 Å, against 140-160 Å in-plane. Out-of-plane geometry is therefore weakly constrained, which is consistent with cFAR 0.17.

Q1: what each map contains
- **J56 (and J61, J63).** Five pieces:
  - A compact lobe (peak 1.0). At half its own peak it encloses only 2.4-3.2k Å^3 (21x17x16 Å). Half-height radius r50 = 7.1 Å at 12 Å. The simulated sfGFP gives 25k Å^3 (48x37x29 Å), r50 about 9-11 Å, and a point source gives r50 = 3.6 Å. The lobe is therefore much more compact than a rigid sfGFP.
  - Segment 1, lobe to a junction, 75-80 Å from the lobe peak. It is weak: minimum 0.10 of lobe peak, mean 0.14.
  - A junction peak (0.26-0.28).
  - A far arm from the junction: 95-104 Å to half-max, plateau 0.15-0.17, ending in a tip peak of about 0.4.
  - Total path from lobe peak to the far end at half-max: 173-180 Å. The bend at the junction is 50-60° over a ±20 Å window, or 80-84° between straight lines fitted to the two segments.
  - Two further features. A second "down arm" leaves the lobe: 86-96 Å to its tip, about 100 Å to half-max, plateau about 0.17-0.2, about 40° from segment 1. A stub continues segment 1 about 15 Å past the junction, so segment 1 plus stub is about 92 Å from the lobe peak.
  - The down arm joins the lobe at 0.13 of max. The junction-plus-far-arm rod joins everything else only at 0.10-0.11.
  - All numbers vary by no more than ±5 Å and ±5° across the 60k-130k contours and between 12 and 15 Å.
- **J51.** The same lobe (r50 7.2 Å, 2.5k Å^3). Segment 1 is 74-80 Å and much stronger (mean 0.31, minimum 0.21). The junction is strong (0.42-0.49). The far arm is weaker and shorter: plateau 0.19-0.21, 81-85 Å past the kink. Lobe peak to far end is 159-161 Å, with a line-fit angle of 82-87°. The far arm only connects below about 0.11 of max (enclosed volume about 63k). There is a weak ridge along the down-arm path: 0.15 at 60 Å out, 0.09 at 80 Å, against 0.17-0.18 in J56.
- **J53 (reference-free, lone-dot-haze particles).** A compact lobe (r50 7.3 Å) with a kink about 28-30 Å out (line-fit angle 60-76°), then a rod of about 95 Å. Lobe peak to far half-max is 122-126 Å, rod plateau 0.26-0.31. There are also short arms of 36-45 Å and 55-73 Å. Its DNA-region CC with J56 is -0.03, so the architecture is different.
- **J52 and J39 (free rods).** Each has a straight rod with no internal bend above 25°, measuring 112-119 Å end-to-end at half-max (after the 5 Å correction, about 107-114 Å, or about 32 bp). Each also has a compact blob:
  - Blob peak 0.87-0.90 of the map maximum, r50 6.2-7.0 Å.
  - At half its own peak, 1.7-2.4k Å^3 (20x15x13 to 21x17x16 Å).
  - Its centre sits 47-49 Å off the rod path. Peak to kink is 46-52 Å; line-fit angle 57-70°; kink to far rod end 84-103 Å; blob peak to far end 136-151 Å.
  - The bridge between blob and rod is weak: minimum 0.10 in J52 and 0.21 in J39, i.e. 16% and 43% of the rod plateau.
  - The two maps agree: CC 0.86-0.87, and the alignment is unique (next distinct solution is 0.75).

Q2: is the far arm in the reference-free map?
- **Yes, the far arm is present in J51.** Along the J56 path its mean density is 0.22 of J51's own lobe peak (J56: 0.18). Its cross-section is peaked and 10-18 Å wide, the shape of a rod rather than haze. J51's background (mean + 3 SD) is 0.009.
- **The tip is not in J51.** The density over the last 17 Å before the far end is 0.18 in J51 but 0.38 in J56, and J56's far half-max end lies about 15-20 Å further out.
- **J56's own starting reference had a shorter far arm.** J55 class 0 (the J51-derived hetero class that J56 started from) has far arm 0.12 and tip 0.05. Its total is 136-144 Å, and its DNA-only CC with J56 is 0.18. J56 iteration 0 (refinement started at 20 Å) already shows the tip at 0.31 and a total of 175-180 Å. So the extra length grew beyond what the reference contained, which argues against simple reference imposition.
- **The provenance chain is unstable.** Lobe-to-far-end length runs 160 (J51), then 140 (J55 class 0), then 178 Å (J56). That spread of about 40 Å is a direct measure of how poorly the DNA path is determined.
- **J61 and J63 are near-identical to J56.** CC to J56 is 0.996 for each. In the DNA region (lobe excluded) the CC is 0.993-0.994, the J63/J61 DNA-integral ratio is 0.98, and the largest J61-J63 difference is ±0.04 against rod plateaus of 0.15-0.4. With shared J56 poses (and hetero-class selection upstream), this is expected whether the haze particles truly carry the same DNA or whether pose imposition rebuilds reference features from weak or noisy signal. It therefore does not validate the arms. What it does show is that the 2D labels "dot-on-rod" and "lone dot + haze" do not separate different 3D content under these poses. Half-map noise is tiny (σ about 0.003 of lobe peak, half-map CC 0.999) and says nothing about bias. Reference-free J53, built from the same haze pool, gives a different architecture (DNA CC -0.03).

Q3: do dot-on-rod and free-rod maps share an architecture?
- **Only loosely.** Both are "compact density, connector, kink, rod". The measurements differ by more than the contour and filter sensitivity:

| Measure | J56 / J51 | J52 / J39 |
|---|---|---|
| Connector length | 75-80 Å | 46-52 Å |
| Line-fit kink angle | 80-87° | 57-70° |
| Connector strength (fraction of rod plateau) | 0.63-1.1 | 0.16-0.43 |
| Peak to far end | 159-180 Å | 136-151 Å |

- **The overlays are not reliable.** Whole-map alignment of J52 or J39 onto J56 has no unique solution: the top five distinct solutions are within 0.013-0.05 CC. DNA-region CC is only 0.24-0.31, so any visual overlay is unreliable.
- **Implied total DNA path.**
  - J56: 173-180 Å, minus the distance from lobe centre to the DNA attachment point (about 15-30 Å) and the 5 Å bias, gives about 140-160 Å.
  - J51: about 125-140 Å.
  - Free rods: 107-114 Å for the rod alone. Adding the blob and its gap, if those are DNA, gives about 140-155 Å.
- **Could the free-rod blob be an sfGFP?** It cannot be excluded, but it does not fit a rigidly bound, fully occupied sfGFP:
  - Its peak height (0.9 of the rod) is about what sfGFP should give against DNA. The simulation gives 0.8 with mass weighting and less once DNA's higher contrast is included.
  - Its integrated density is only 31-35 Å-of-rod equivalents. A full sfGFP would be 56-113, so the blob is about 30-60% of one.
  - Its half-max envelope is about 10x smaller in volume than a simulated sfGFP.
  - It is roughly isotropic, so it is not a straight DNA piece about 33 Å long lying in the map.
  - The readings that fit are a partly occupied or orientationally blurred sfGFP, or a blurred or bent DNA end. Its mass happens to match the rod's shortfall from 170 Å, which is suggestive but not decisive.
- **The same mass test applied to J56.** J56's lobe holds 153-203 rod-equivalents (J51: 106-160), against 56-113 expected for sfGFP with fully occupied rigid DNA. Its rods sit at 0.15-0.18 of lobe peak, where a rigid model gives 0.8-1.2. Either the DNA is 2-3x under-represented (heterogeneity or flexibility) or the lobe is not a single rigid sfGFP.

Q4: attached DNA length versus a 50 bp duplex
- **If segment 1 and the far arm are one continuous duplex,** J56 implies about 140-160 Å, i.e. 0-30 Å shorter than 170 Å. J51 implies about 125-140 Å; J55 class 0 about 110-125 Å.
- **The "short" reading cannot be excluded either.** The junction carries 1.7x (J56) to 2.3x (J51) the far-arm density. A simulated continuous duplex kinked by 55-80° gives only 1.1-1.2x, so there is extra overlapping density there. The lobe also has two arms of about 90 Å. If the attached DNA is just one of those arms and the far arm is a superposed or separate molecule, the attached DNA would be about 70-80 Å.
- **The free-rod maps do not offer a 50 bp benchmark.** Their rods are themselves only about 110 Å (about 32 bp equivalent), not 170 Å.
- **Net: the maps do not decide shorter vs equal vs full length.** The deficit relative to 170 Å (0-30 Å) is smaller than the processing-dependent spread (about 40 Å) and the attachment-point uncertainty (15-30 Å).

undecidable: Whether segment 1 plus the far arm in J56 is one continuous kinked duplex, or a superposition of alternative arm positions or extra molecules. The junction density excess (1.7-2.3x against 1.1-1.2x for a kinked duplex) and the two ~90 Å arms from the lobe support the superposition reading as much as the continuous one.

Whether DNA attached to sfGFP is shorter than, equal to, or as long as 50 bp. The implied deficit (0-30 Å for the continuous reading, about 90 Å for the single-arm reading) is within the processing-chain spread (about 40 Å: J55 class 0 140, J51 160, J56 178 Å) plus the 15-30 Å uncertainty in where the DNA attaches to the lobe.

Whether the lobe is a single sfGFP. It is about 10x smaller in half-max volume than a rigid sfGFP at 12 Å and carries 1.5-3x more integrated density relative to the rods than expected, so it could be a blurred or partly occupied sfGFP with under-represented DNA, or a denser or different object.

Whether the free-rod blob is an sfGFP. Its peak height fits, but its mass is 30-60% of one, its size is about 10x too small, and it is joined to the rod only weakly. A partly occupied or blurred sfGFP and a blurred or bent DNA end are both consistent.

Out-of-plane tilt of any segment, and so true 3D contour lengths. All maps are planar to 35-47 Å thickness and the anisotropy (cFAR 0.17) suppresses the out-of-plane direction, so the measured lengths are effectively in-plane values or lower bounds.

Whether the J61/J63 agreement reflects real DNA in the haze particles or pose-driven reference bias. Shared J56 poses plus hetero-class selection make the agreement expected either way; a junk or ice-class reconstruct-only with the same poses, or a per-subset local refinement, would be needed.

Whether the free-rod and dot-on-rod maps share one DNA architecture. Both have a blob-connector-kink-rod topology, but connector length (50 vs 77 Å) and kink angle (57-70° vs 80-87°) differ, and whole-map alignments are not unique.
Why the free rods are only about 110 Å rather than about 170 Å: frayed or flexible ends averaged out, genuinely shorter or partly degraded duplexes, or DNA continuing into the blob.
